children: West Red Lake Gold Mines Ltd.
announces its financial and operating results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 (“

”) located in the Red Lake mining district of Ontario. The Company will hold a webcast on November 30, 2026 to discuss the results. Please refer to the webcast details provided near the end of this news release for information on how to attend.
Gold production totaled 7,859 ounces during Q3, bringing year-to-date production to 22,102 ounces.
Gold sales totaled 7,737 ounces during Q3, bringing year-to-date gold sales to 22,162 ounces.
Revenue totaled $45.8 million and income from mine operations of $12.7 million, representing an operating margin of 28%.
Adjusted net earnings(2) of $5.5 million, or $0.01 per basic share, bringing year-to-date adjusted net earnings of $24.5 million, or $0.06 per basic share.
Adjusted EBITDA(2) of $15.6 million, bringing year-to-date adjusted EBITDA to $52.1 million.
Cash costs(1)(2) of US$2,400 per ounce sold and All-in sustaining costs (“
”)(1)(2) of US$3,985(1) per ounce sold, reflecting lower gold production and sales during the quarter.
Generated $1.9 million in positive free cash flow, marking the second consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow.
The Company ended the quarter with approximately $18.8 million in cash and cash equivalents.
Shane Williams, President and CEO, commented,

“Madsen continued to generate positive free cash flow in the third quarter, bringing year-to-date revenue to $136.6 million, adjusted EBITDA to $52.1 million and free cash flow to $5.4 million in our first nine months of commercial production. Although underground mining challenges impacted production and unit costs during the quarter, we continued to advance key operational and infrastructure initiatives to support improved operating performance.”

“Our immediate focus remains on improving underground mining productivity and advancing development to establish additional mining fronts. During the quarter, we supplemented our underground workforce with specialized contractors, commissioned the secondary crusher and continued to invest in underground development and infrastructure.”

“As we advance access to new mining areas, including the 904 Complex and the Fork deposit, we expect to benefit from greater operating flexibility and a more consistent production profile as we move into 2027. Our recently announced Integrated Pre-Feasibility Study builds on these investments and defines a clear pathway to growing production and extending mine life, with Madsen serving as the central hub of our district-scale strategy in Red Lake.”
Financial key results for nine months ended September 30, 2026
(expressed in thousands of Canadian dollars, unless otherwise stated)
Financial performance during Q3 reflected lower gold production and sales relative to the three months ended June 30, 2026 (“

”), together with higher unit operating costs and sustaining capital expenditures. Despite these challenges, the Company maintained positive operating margins and generated positive free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter.

Gold sales totaled 7,737 ounces during Q3 at an average realized gold price of US$4,230 per ounce, generating revenue of $45.8 million, compared with $49.0 million in Q2. Income from mining operations totaled $12.7 million, with an operating margin of 28%, compared with $20.1 million and 41%, respectively, in Q2.

Adjusted EBITDA totaled $15.6 million, compared with $22.1 million in Q2, while adjusted net earnings totaled $5.5 million, or $0.01 per basic share, compared with $12.6 million, or $0.03 per basic share, in Q2.

Cash costs increased to US$2,400 per ounce sold, compared with US$2,000 per ounce in Q2. AISC increased to US$3,985 per ounce sold, compared with US$3,284 per ounce in Q2, lower gold sales and an increase in sustaining capital expenditures to $14.5 million from $12.3 million in Q2.

The Company generated $1.9 million of positive free cash flow during Q3, bringing year-to-date free cash flow to $5.4 million. The Company ended the quarter with approximately $18.8 million in cash and cash equivalents.
During the first nine months of commercial production at Madsen, the Company generated $136.6 million in revenue, $48.1 million in income from mining operations and $52.1 million in adjusted EBITDA.
As reported in the Company's operational update dated October 27, 2026 (
), gold production totaled 7,859 ounces during Q3, bringing year-to-date production to 22,102 ounces.

During Q3, the Company mined 63,945 tonnes at an average grade of 3.8 g/t Au, compared with 74,604 tonnes at 4.1 g/t Au in Q2. Underground mining performance was impacted by the complexities associated with remnant pillar extraction and the availability of skilled underground personnel. Specialized contractors were brought in to support mining activities and maintain development progress.
Mill performance continued to improve, with average throughput increasing to 867 tonnes per day (“

”) from 842 tpd in Q2, while gold recovery averaged 94%. The commissioning of the secondary crusher during Q3 addressed material-handling constraints and supported increased processing capacity. Lower-grade ore stockpiled during Q2 was also processed during the quarter.
Underground development progressed during Q3, with a focus on expanding production inventory and establishing additional mining fronts. Continued development toward non-remanent areas.
The Company remains on track to achieve its revised 2026 gold production guidance of 27,000 to 32,000 ounces.

For the balance of 2026, the Company will continue to invest in underground development and infrastructure, together with the transition into new mining areas, including the 904 Complex and the Fork deposit, expected to provide greater operating flexibility and support a more consistent production profile in 2027.

Management will host a webcast to discuss the results on Monday, November 30, 2026, commencing at 8:00 am PT (Vancouver time) / 10:00 am ET. Registration will open 20 minutes prior to the event start time.
The Company’s unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial statements for the three, six and nine months ended September 30, 2026 (“
”) and related management’s discussion and analysis (“

”) are available for download on the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the Company’s website at www.westredlakegold.com. All financial figures are expressed in Canadian dollars (‘C$), unless otherwise indicated.

The technical information presented in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Will Robinson, P.Geo., Vice President of Exploration for West Red Lake Gold and the Qualified Person for exploration at the West Red Lake Project, and by Hayley Halsall-Whitney, P.Eng., Vice President of Operations for West Red Lake Gold and the Qualified Person for technical services at the West Red Lake Project, as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.
About West Red Lake Gold Mines

West Red Lake Gold Mines Ltd. is a Canadian gold producer and developer advancing a high-grade, district scale opportunity in the Red Lake district of Ontario. The Company’s flagship Madsen Mine has recently achieved commercial production and is positioned as the central hub of a growing multi asset platform. The Company controls a 47 km² land package in one of the world’s most prolific mining districts, which has historically produced over 20 million ounces of gold from high grade systems1. West Red Lake also owns the Rowan Property in Red Lake, covering 31 km² that includes three past producing mines (Rowan, Mount Jamie and Red Summit) and represents a key source of future production growth.
